title: Saving Faith
speaker: Mr. Steve Thomas

outline.title: The Nature and Origin of Saving Faith
subpoints: Faith is a grace and gift of God, not of human origin
It is the work of the Spirit of Christ in the hearts of the elect
Its effect is the saving of the soul

outline.title: The Means of Faith
subpoints: Ordinarily wrought by the ministry of the Word
Increased and strengthened by sacraments and prayer
Faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God

outline.title: Faith vs. Knowledge
subpoints: Faith is affirmation of truth without direct sensory evidence
Faith is reasonable and based on evidence, not an irrational leap
Faith and reason complement each other in God's design

outline.title: The Acts of Saving Faith
subpoints: Believing the truth of God's Word for His authority
Yielding obedience to commands and embracing promises
Accepting, receiving, and resting upon Christ alone for justification, sanctification, and eternal life

outline.title: The Growth and Assurance of Faith
subpoints: Faith varies in degree and can be weakened
It grows to full assurance through Christ, the author and finisher of faith
Encouragement from the examples of faith in Hebrews 11

summary:
This lesson, part of a series on the Ordo Salutis (Order of Salvation), examines the theological concept of saving faith as defined in Chapter 14 of the Westminster Confession of Faith. The teaching begins by establishing that saving faith is a grace and a gift from God, not a human achievement. It is the work of the Holy Spirit in the hearts of the elect, enabling them to believe to the saving of their souls. The sermon clarifies that while faith is exercised by the believer, its origin is entirely divine, countering the notion that humans can generate saving faith on their own.

The speaker distinguishes between faith and knowledge, arguing that faith is not an irrational leap but a reasonable affirmation of truth based on evidence, such as the testimony of Scripture and the consistency of historical and geographical facts. Using the example of the city of Jerusalem, the lesson illustrates that faith demands evidence and complements human reason rather than contradicting it. This perspective encourages believers to view their faith as grounded and rational.

The ordinary means by which this faith is wrought is identified as the ministry of the Word, supported by the sacraments and prayer. The lesson then moves to the specific acts of saving faith: believing the truth of God's Word, yielding obedience to its commands, and, most principally, accepting, receiving, and resting upon Christ alone for justification, sanctification, and eternal life. The sermon concludes by noting that while faith can be weak or strong and may face trials, it grows in the believer through the work of Christ, who is both the author and finisher of their faith, offering encouragement through the examples of faith found in Hebrews 11.
